tldr: Headlines uniformly report Russian aerial strikes killing civilians in Zaporizhzhia, but the dominant international editorial choice is to bracket the death toll with the Trump-Putin diesel deal — a causal juxtaposition absent from Ukrainian outlets, which focus on weapons and rising casualty counts alone.

single_outlet_findings.finding: The only headline to use the editorial verdict 'backfires' — assigning negative consequence to Trump's diesel deal — where other outlets in the same POLITICAL frame merely establish temporal sequence ('after Trump strikes diesel deal').

The only headline to explicitly channel Zelenskyy's accusation that the strikes are Russia's 'thanks' for the US sanctions lift, foregrounding the causal-culpability framing rather than the body count or deal-chronology.

bottom_line: The headline layer presents the Zaporizhzhia strikes as a Russian military attack on civilians, but the majority of international outlets construct an implicit indictment of the Trump-Putin diesel deal by placing it in immediate causal proximity to the death toll — a frame Ukrainian outlets, focused on weaponry and rising casualty numbers, do not adopt.
